candidates.name: Slack-telescoped multilevel estimator in one shared O(log n)-bit environment
candidates.statement: At budget M, sum over m of conditional-walk averages (walk length l(M-m)) of T_{b,m}-T_{b,m-1}; means telescope, differences have norm 2^{-p+C0 d} so O(d)-length walks suppress noise to 2^{-p-K_n d}; descriptors O(d) bits, children at budget <= M-d; integrated (all-vertex, retention-weighted) L_s errors; the final factor N is paid by p=Theta(log n).

neighbours.ref: Multilevel Monte Carlo (Heinrich 2001; Giles, Oper. Res. 2008) [from memory]
neighbours.relation: telescoping sum over levels; differences of consecutive levels have small variance, so fewer samples are needed at fine levels
neighbours.verdict: close variant of the core principle (transfer); MLMC has no space/recursion-depth role

test3.evidence: It is what makes per-level space O(slack) so that the allowance telescoping (I28) closes at O(log n). Lean: IterationSchedule.lean ('decomposition of estimator increments'), HierarchicalEstimator.lean (error induction; Net.error_estimate dominated share 0.12), EstimatorBounds.lean.

final.justification: The telescoping-differences principle is MLMC (an existing concept from numerical probability, so its import is transfer), and CDST23 already varies precision across recursion levels for the same purpose. The concrete space-accounting coupling is new, but under the strict rule it is a close variant. Upgrade to N3 only if test 4 shows hard discoverability given MLMC and CDST23 in L.

P-C1.hide: Sections 3 onward (hierarchy, atoms, estimator, ... ) - i.e. I06-I12 and everything downstream; keep Sec. 2 (configuration reduction).
P-C1.prompt: Given p0=(I-S)^{-1}e for a strictly forward substochastic S on poly(n) vertices, propose a sequence of O(log n) transformations producing an exact or one-sided-approximate representation of p0(x0) in which transition entries become uniformly small, suitable for estimation by short random seeds. State the transformation and its invariant.
P-C1.equivalence: Judge accepts if the proposal contains all of: (a) a correction moving transition mass into a reward via a factorization (I+E)(I-C) or equivalent; (b) duplication of vertices/destinations to split large entries; (c) control that support grows by a bounded factor while max entry shrinks geometrically, giving O(log n) stages. Partial credit (a) only = Richardson (expected high rate, negative control).
P-C1.lean_check: Optional: state ProbabilityHierarchy.lean's per-stage contract (SB bounds, residual, copyZone) and test whether a proposal's definitions satisfy it.

P-C2.hide: Sections 7-12 (additive schedule, compression, fingerprints, controller) given the hierarchy and atoms.
P-C2.prompt: Given row-bounded stochastic tables in a shared O(log n)-bit environment and conditional-averaging walks with uniform gap, design a recursive estimator whose per-level space is not Theta(log n), so total space is O(log n).
P-C2.equivalence: Accept if the proposal telescopes estimates across consecutive budgets/precisions and ties averaging length and frame size to the budget decrease (slack), with total space summing to O(log n). Record separately proposals that cite MLMC or CDST23 explicitly.
P-C2.contamination_note: MLMC and CDST23 are in L (the latter cited); the test measures whether the space coupling is found, not the principle.
